title: Victim compensation scheme - an underused remedy in criminal cases
p1:
Many crime victims fight for justice but miss out on a support system that already exists.

A court case may punish the offender, but who helps the victim recover from the financial and emotional impact?
p2: A common misconception is that victims can only seek compensation through a separate civil case. In reality, criminal law also provides a victim compensation scheme where eligible victims or their families can receive financial assistance from the state.
p3:
This scheme can help survivors of serious crimes such as assault, sexual offences, and other forms of violence with expenses related to recovery, rehabilitation, or loss suffered.

The surprising part? Many eligible victims are unaware that they can apply for this relief, and compensation is not dependent on the offender being able to pay.

Knowing about this remedy can make a real difference when rebuilding life after a crime.
conclusion: Do you think more victims would seek justice if they were made aware of compensation schemes available to them?
